message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for predicting a binary outcome (e.g., yes/no, success/failure) based on one or more predictor variables. It models the probability that the dependent variable belongs to a particular category by applying the logistic function to a linear combination of the predictors. The model’s parameters are typically estimated using maximum likelihood estimation, and the resulting coefficients can be interpreted in terms of odds ratios. Logistic regression can also be extended to handle multiple categories (multinomial logistic regression) or ordered outcomes (ordinal logistic regression).
